title: Physical Pixel
description: Turn an LED on and off by typing H or L on your computer.

steps.clip: Grab an Arduino Uno and its USB cable, a breadboard, 220 Ω resistor, LED and a few jumper wires.
Push a 220 Ω resistor into the breadboard, its two legs in two different numbered columns.
hints: A resistor works either way round.
It protects the LED: without it too much current flows and the LED burns out.
steps.goal: Put the resistor for the LED on the breadboard.

steps.clip: A jumper wire from one of the resistor's columns to pin 13 on the Arduino.
hints: Pin 13 is on the Arduino's row of numbered sockets.
Any free hole in that column works.

steps.clip: Now the LED: its long leg in the same column as the resistor's other leg, its short leg in an empty column right next to it.
hints: The long leg is + (the anode) — it must face the resistor or the LED stays dark.
Legs in the same column are already connected.
steps.goal: Connect the LED's long leg (+) to the resistor.

steps.clip: A jumper wire from the short leg's column to the − (blue) row along the bottom edge — and, since this is the first thing using it, one more wire from that − row to a GND pin on the Arduino (now the whole row is GND).
hints: The − row is already joined to GND.
steps.goal: Connect the LED's short leg (−) to GND.

steps.clip: Copy the code into the Arduino IDE and click Upload. In the Serial Monitor type H and press Enter: the LED turns on. Type L: it turns off.
